title: horizon-transport-inference-field-notes
body:
Purpose: quick scratchpad from kickoff + technical sync with Horizon Transport (HT) — internal capture for follow-ups, assumptions, and quick cost/ops notes.

Attendees (HT): Maya Reddy (CTO), Oliver Park (Platform), Lina Gomez (DataOps)
Redwood side: Priya (lead SE), Diego (infra), Samir (runtime perf)
Meeting date: 2024-10-11 (initial), follow-up 2024-10-28

One-line ask from HT: move prototype from API calls to private on-prem inference cluster for 24/7 routing decisions (low latency, offline resilience) — target P99 <= 80ms for 512-token sequences.

High-level constraints / environment notes:
- On-prem site: primary cluster in their EU datacenter (Equinix) behind strict egress rules. Customer will not allow outbound model weights download from public internet.
- Network: NAT-only egress through corp proxy; need static IP allowlist for Redwood control plane (if we use private control plane) or fully air-gapped option.
- Security: SOC2 + ISO27001; they want KMS integration (Azure Key Vault) and audit logs forwarded to their Splunk instance.
- Hardware: they plan to provision 4x A30-equivalent nodes initially (customer language), want Redwood to advise sizing.
- Peak load: expected 120 RR (requests per second) for inference, modal burst 300 RPS for 5–10m windows during routing peaks. Avg prompt length ~160 tokens, output ~40 tokens.

Technical implications / gotchas (observed in call):
- KV-cache warmup will be important: many requests share similar prefixes (routing prompts). Need to prototype prefix caching + sticky routing to preserve cache locality.
- Batching tradeoffs: to hit P99 80ms for 512 tokens we need conservative batching; suggest enabling dynamic batching with per-route SLOs and a fallback to single-request path for high-priority messages.
- Quantization: customer wants to keep FP16 for quality initially; they are open to 4-bit for cost if we show evals.
- Model choice: HT currently using a 7B-chat open model. Mismatch between 'developer convenience' and 'latency SLO' — discuss trimmed instruction tuning or distilled variant later.
- Networking: on-prem NAT + corporate proxy may break kernel ops that fetch runtime telemetry. Need ops plan: either allow Redwood collector IPs (we get a static egress list) or deploy local collector with periodic batched push to their Splunk — they prefer local collector.

Rough sizing/calculation (very rough, SDR-level):
- Given token/prompt numbers: 120 steady RPS * (160+40)=200 tokens/request -> 24k tokens/s steady. At 300 burst RPS -> 60k tokens/s.
- If using 7B FP16 runtime, ballpark throughput per A30 equiv node (with our runtime and 512-seq) ~4–8k tokens/s depending on batching — need 4–8 nodes. They have 4 nodes planned; recommend 6 nodes for headroom+cache locality. (Action: Diego to run a small perf sim with current 7B model binary on 4/6 nodes to validate).

Operational notes + rollout options:
- Private deployment flavors discussed: 1) Private control plane (Redwood-managed control plane + customer data plane) 2) Fully private (air-gapped) package with local control plane (longer procurement). HT prefers private control plane if we can get static egress allowlist and KMS integration.
- Canary plan: start with a shadow traffic run for 2 weeks (no returns to customers), then 5% traffic for 1 week, then 25% after monitoring. Need auto-fallback to hosted model in case of node failure (they may not want outbound, so fallback option limited).

Open questions (to resolve before proposal):
- Legal / contract: do they accept our private control plane T&Cs? (Sales to confirm).
- KMS: do they want Redwood to hold any keys? They prefer customer-managed keys in Azure Key Vault; engineering to confirm integration path. (Jira ticket assigned).
- Audit pipeline: confirm Splunk ingestion format and retention SLA.
- Telemetry: what metrics/retention do they need? (They flagged trace-level for 90 days — estimate storage needed).

Immediate action items (owners + ETA):
- Diego: run perf simulation for 7B FP16 on 4 vs 6 A30-eq nodes, capture tokens/s and P95/P99 estimates. ETA: 2024-10-18. (JIRA-ENGINF-879 assigned).
- Priya: draft test plan for prefix caching experiment + list of representative prompt clusters from HT (they will share sample dataset). ETA: 2024-10-20.
- Samir: prepare a short A/B eval comparing FP16 vs 4-bit quant on 7B model for 5 sample prompts (quality delta, latency). ETA: 2024-10-22.
- Sales (linked): confirm legal appetite for private control plane and summarize any mandatory contract clauses. ETA: EOD 2024-10-23.
- Ops: design local telemetry collector spec for Splunk push and confirm network port requirements. Diego to own with Ops. ETA: 2024-10-25.

Notes to self (informal):
- Need to push HT to share a small corpus of actual prompts (not sanitized) — will help with cache strategy.
- Watch out for their strict egress policy — if we can't get even static IP allowlist we must plan for fully air-gapped installer (longer lead).
- Consider recommending a trimmed instruction set model variant to shave few ms on attention. Samir thinks distillation could help but requires Evals bench.

Sample prompts (copied from call voice):
1) "Given vehicle telemetry X and route constraints Y, produce top-3 reroute options with ETA deltas and confidence scores."
2) "Summarize driver message and extract urgency label + next action."

Meeting artifacts to attach in proposal:
- Perf sim outputs (Diego)
- Eval report (Samir)
- Network/ops spec (Ops)
- Sample prompt clusters (HT)

Longer-term ideas (brainstorm):
- Edge-microservice: run tiny model on-device for immediate safety checks; backfill with full model in DC for optimization suggestions.
- Persistent KV-store per-vehicle to speed up repeated queries for same route segments.

Next check-in: 2024-10-28 follow-up call (schedule pending) — goal: firm up node count + KMS path so Sales can finalize SOW.

Random scratch flags (for later cleanup):
- confirm GCC/region compliance? HT has some EU-reg customers; check data residency clause.
- ask product team whether Canary policy can use token-budget based throttling (not just percent).

End notes: quick and messy — will convert to a cleaner SOW appendix once perf numbers come in.
